cim: How 7 restaurant chains are using AI
cim_eredeti: How 7 restaurant chains are using AI
szoveg_eredeti:
Major restaurant chains from Bojangles to White Castle and McDonald’s are turning to artificial intelligence to reduce labor hours and improve the customer experience.

On Thursday, Anthropic, the company behind Claude and a host of other artificial intelligence tools, debuted on public markets with a valuation well north of $1 trillion, heralding the maturity of the artificial intelligence sector.

This year has seen an increase in the adoption of AI tools by major restaurant chains, as the technology, which boosters have promised for years would revolutionize restaurants, reaches something like operational maturity. While there have been major restaurant flops — Starbucks’ AI stockkeeper lasted all of nine months — AI tools seem to be making steady gains in restaurants.

In the last three months, no fewer than seven major restaurant companies have announced significant expansions of their AI toolsets. To list just a few: McDonald’s wants to deploy bilingual drive-thru voice AI by the end of next year; Taco Bell plans to have similar ordering tech live in 1,500 stores by the end of 2026; and Wonder deployed its first instance of an automated makeline, based on tech it acquired from Sweetgreen.

Here seven of the major shifts towards AI adoption in the restaurant sector from recent months:

Hi Auto's technology is now at 267 restaurants and is on its way toward reaching half of the system by early next year. Read the full article ➔

The fast food giant says the automated ordering system could save 50 weekly labor hours, but some franchisees are unsure if the technology is something customers want or if it can improve hospitality. Read the full article ➔

Yum Brands hopes continued marketing magic at Taco Bell, menu investments at KFC and overall tech improvements will result in strong sales growth. Read the full article ➔

Hi Auto’s voice ordering tech processes 1 million orders a week across 500 Bojangles restaurants with 98% accuracy, the chain said. Read the full article ➔

The food hall company will use the tech it acquired from Sweetgreen for $186 million to offer lower prices, extended hours and expand into new markets. Read the full article ➔

A partnership with retail tech company T-ROC Global could help CPK reverse the steady erosion of its storebase by bringing the brand to more consumers. Read the full article ➔

A partnership with Automated Retail Technologies will bring fresh items from the burger QSR’s menu to select large-format stores. Read the full article ➔
